testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure used to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the brake lines. Air brakes do not work instantly. There is usually a delay of at least half a second between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes beginning to work.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, the S-cam:

options.text: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum
Pushes the brake shoes against the brake linings
Pushes the brake linings against the wheel axles

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction that slows the vehicle.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks
Each system has its own separate air tanks
You must choose which system to use

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own separate air tanks
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share the brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: The leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should not exceed ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 psi
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle, air should not leak more than 5 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle should not be driven because repairs are needed.

questions.question: Warning lights that show anti-lock brakes are not working are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lights. These lights show when there is a problem with the braking system.

questions.question: On flat surfaces, wheel chocks:

options.text: Stop a parked vehicle from rolling
Make a parked vehicle easier to move
Should only be used on the front driver's side tire

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop a parked vehicle from rolling
questions.explanation: When you cannot use the parking brake, wheel chocks can hold a parked vehicle in place on a flat surface.

questions.question: An application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is pushing on the brakes right now
How much air pressure is available in the system
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is pushing on the brakes right now
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows the actual air pressure being used on the brakes at any moment. This helps drivers notice if their brakes are starting to fail.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the driver should:

options.text: Warm up the vehicle before driving so fuel reaches the engine
Wait for the air compressor to reach at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems before driving
Start driving right after the vehicle starts

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the air compressor to reach at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems before driving
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build pressure to at least 100 psi in both systems. Watch the pressure gauges to check the levels.

questions.question: Brakes that are out of adjustment will:

options.text: Force some brakes to work too hard and fail

questions.correctAnswerText: Force some brakes to work too hard and fail
questions.explanation: Brakes out of adjustment will wear out and fail faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: Not draining air tanks can cause:

options.text: Water to freeze and cause brake failure
Too much air to build up in the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Water to freeze and cause brake failure
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. If water is left in the tanks, it can freeze in cold weather and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: A visual low pressure warning signal should activate before air pressure drops to what level?
questions.correctAnswerText: 55 to 75 psi
questions.explanation: A visual low pressure warning signal should activate before air pressure drops to 55 to 75 psi. The signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air?

options.text: The air pressure has become too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure has become too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air from the tanks when pressure gets too high. If the valve operates, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: When air pressure reaches 125 psi, what does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Stops the compressor from pumping air
Begins pumping air into the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops the compressor from pumping air
questions.explanation: When air pressure reaches about 125 psi, the governor stops the compressor from pumping air. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: They should not be used in cold weather
They remove water and oil from the air tanks
They move air to the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the air tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that can damage the brake system if it builds up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove this water and oil.

questions.question: Do not drive if a brake drum has cracks larger than what fraction of the friction area width?
questions.correctAnswerText: One half
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums during your walk-around inspection before each trip. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, what gear should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: A lower gear
questions.explanation: Before going downhill, shift to a lower gear. Gravity will cause your vehicle to speed up as you go downhill.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, what is the maximum air leakage allowed in one minute during an applied leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 4 psi
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should have no more than 4 psi air loss per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks
It moves air to the back of the truck

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the air storage tanks
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: What makes up the emergency brake system?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three brake systems: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What is activated by an electric switch triggered by the brake pedal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake lights
questions.explanation: When you push the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if your brakes are hot. Let them cool first. Using the parking brake when brakes are hot can damage them.

questions.question: Brakes can get out of adjustment quickly, especially:
questions.correctAnswerText: If they are hot.
questions.explanation: Hot brakes lose adjustment quickly. Check your brakes regularly. Your vehicle needs all brakes working and adjusted correctly to stop safely.

questions.question: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ malfunction lamps to show when the ABS is not working.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: ABS vehicles have yellow malfunction lamps. These warn you when the braking system is not working. Find the malfunction lamp in your vehicle before you drive.

questions.question: ABS brakes:

options.text: Prevent your vehicle from accelerating when going uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid wheel lockup.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) stop your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.correctAnswerText: One inch
questions.explanation: Before driving, check the slack adjusters. Park the vehicle, set wheel chocks, and release the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster. It should not move more than one inch. If it moves more, the adjuster needs repair.
